sentences.text: Pulchrapollia was a small bird roughly the size of a red-fronted parakeet.
It possessed zygodactyl feet, a foot structure where two toes point forward and two point backward.
The holotype fossil, the specimen the species is based on, was discovered in 1978 near Walton-on-the-Naze in the London Clay.
Dyke and Cooper described the type species Pulchrapollia gracilis in 2000.
Mayr and Kitchener later described the species Pulchrapollia tenuipes in 2023.
Halcyornithids, the family to which Pulchrapollia belongs, are considered basal relatives of both parrots and songbirds.
Pulchrapollia was initially classified as a stem-parrot distinct from the Halcyornithidae family.
Pulchrapollia lived during the Early Eocene in the United Kingdom and the United States.
Researchers suggest that the smaller braincase of Pulchrapollia compared to other halcyornithids might represent an increase in encephalization over time.
